title: Average restriction covariance
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate $j\in\mathrm{Fin}\ n$. For independent $\omega,\omega'\sim\pi$, replace coordinate $j$ in the inputs to $f$ and $g$ by $\omega$ and $\omega'$, respectively; the average restriction covariance is the expectation of the product covariance of these two resulting functions over the remaining coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
caveat: The supplied statement does not include the definitions of product covariance or coordinate replacement, so their precise conventions cannot be recovered here.
